extra.message: User-controlled courseCode and since are interpolated directly into a raw SQL WHERE clause passed to db.execute(sql.raw(...)). Both parameters come from /api/export/submissions query params, allowing SQL injection.

The column name (field) and value are interpolated into sql.raw() without allowlisting or parameterization. Both the field name and value derive from the user-supplied criteria object, enabling SQL injection.
The sortBy value is interpolated directly into the ORDER BY clause of a raw SQL statement. sortBy is supplied by the caller from the 'sort_by' query parameter, allowing SQL injection.

layoutPreset is interpolated into a shell command string and executed via spawn(cmd, { shell: true }). layoutPreset is user-controlled (POST body) and unvalidated, allowing arbitrary command execution.
outputFormat is concatenated into an execSync() command string. outputFormat is user-controlled (POST body) and never validated against an allowlist, allowing command injection (e.g. '; rm -rf /').
The user-supplied 'expression' string is passed to new Function('score','maxPoints', `return ${expression}`). This executes arbitrary JavaScript on the server (code injection / RCE).

completeLegacySsoAction accepts an email and a 'ticket' but only checks the ticket is non-empty; it never verifies the ticket against the identity provider. Any caller can log in as any provisioned user by supplying their email and an arbitrary ticket value, creating a valid session.

completeLtiLaunchAction only checks that an email and launchId are present; it never verifies the LTI launch signature/nonce. Any caller can mint a session for any provisioned user by supplying their email, bypassing authentication.

The instructor-supplied 'label' is concatenated into a filename and joined into the archive path with no basename()/traversal guard. A label such as '../../...' lets an attacker write arbitrary files outside the archive directory (path traversal).

The uploaded file's original name (file.name) is joined directly into the public asset directory and written to disk with no sanitization, MIME check, or size limit. A crafted filename (../...) enables path traversal, and arbitrary content (e.g. HTML/JS) can be written to the public folder.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The 'pack' query parameter is concatenated into a file path (path.join(STARTER_PACKS_DIR, `${pack}.md`)) without basename() sanitization, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files (e.g. pack=../../etc/passwd).
previewCourseResource fetches an arbitrary user-supplied sourceUrl with no protocol/host allowlist. This allows SSRF against internal/cloud metadata endpoints.

restorePortalProfileAction merges the entire user-supplied JSON payload onto the user's DB row via db.update(users).set(fields). An attacker can set arbitrary columns including 'role' (e.g. 'school_admin') or 'isActive', achieving privilege escalation.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: importFieldPlacementNoteAction merges the user-supplied JSON object directly onto the submission via db.update(submissions).set(fields). A TA (review access) can set gradeReleased=true or status='released', bypassing the instructor-only releaseGradeAction.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: updateUserRoleAction only calls requireUser() (any authenticated user) rather than requireRole('school_admin'). Any logged-in user, including students, can change any other user's role to 'school_admin', granting full privilege escalation.

resolveVendorFeedIdentity verifies JWTs while allowing the 'none' algorithm. An attacker can forge an unsigned token asserting an arbitrary vendorId, bypassing authentication for the attendance-hardware-feed endpoint.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: loadNotificationDetail fetches a notification by ID with only requireUser() and no ownership check (unlike the dismiss route which filters by userId). Any authenticated user can read another user's notification, which may contain password-reset links and other sensitive content.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The staff directory endpoint selects all user columns (db.select() with innerJoin) and returns the full user row (r.users), including passwordHash, phone, and bio. Any enrolled viewer receives staff password hashes.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The 'keyword' and 'cachedTrack' values are interpolated directly into an XPath expression without escaping. An attacker can break out of the contains() clause to alter the query (XPath injection), potentially accessing lessons outside their track.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: verifyStaffGroupMembership builds an LDAP filter by interpolating unescaped uid and groupCn values. Unlike findStaffByEmail (which uses ldapEscape), these inputs can inject filter operators to bypass the membership check used to authorize adding a teaching contact.

The 'return_to' query parameter is passed to NextResponse.redirect(new URL(returnTo, req.url)) with no validation. Unlike the cohort-transfers endpoint (which checks startsWith('/')), an attacker can redirect users to an external malicious site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The 'export_label' query parameter is embedded into the Content-Disposition header without stripping CR/LF (the archive route does sanitize). This permits HTTP header injection / response splitting.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The user-controlled 'sections' value is used as a loop bound with no upper limit (the sibling 'sections' route caps at MAX_SECTIONS=25). A huge value causes unbounded CPU/memory consumption and a massive rubric jsonb write.
When context=expanded is passed, the route returns the raw error message and stack trace (err.stack) to the client, leaking server file paths and implementation details to any authenticated caller.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: applyDistrictSettingsOverride recursively merges arbitrary keys from the JSON overrides (including '__proto__' / nested keys) into the shared courseDefaults object, enabling prototype pollution of the server process.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

extra.message: createIntegrationKeyAction generates API key secrets using Math.random() instead of a cryptographically secure source (randomToken/crypto.randomBytes). The predictable key can be guessed, allowing API key forgery.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The '$regex' operator compiles a user-supplied regular expression via new RegExp(String(val)). An attacker can submit a catastrophic backtracking pattern to cause ReDoS/CPU exhaustion.
initializeAccount stores passwords using a single unsalted SHA-1 hash, which is trivially reversible for weak passwords. Imported accounts are protected by an insecure hashing scheme.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: recordSisSyncFailure logs the entire roster record (including the plaintext legacyPassword) to the console via console.error, exposing credentials in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: pushGradeBatchToLegacySis sends the API key as a query parameter over plain HTTP, exposing the credential in transit and in server/proxy logs.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: readReportCardLink verifies the JWT with ignoreExpiration: true, defeating the expiresIn: '30m' set at creation. Guardian report-card links never actually expire.
recordCatalogSearch logs the raw searchQuery without sanitizing newlines (unlike recordDiscussionSearch). A query containing CR/LF lets an attacker forge log entries (log injection).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: The catalog endpoint reflects the caller's Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for any origin, permitting cross-site credentialed reads (overly permissive CORS).

parseDigestPrefsCookie parses the cookie value as XML without rejecting DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations (the safe counterpart rejects them), allowing XML external entity / entity expansion attacks if the underlying parser supports them.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: openGradeDraft uses unauthenticated AES-256-CBC. Combined with the grade-draft endpoint returning distinct errors for padding vs format failures (422 vs 400), this forms a padding oracle enabling decryption/forgery of grade drafts.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: resolvePartnerAssertedRole uses loose equality and a truthy check (Boolean(hint.access)) on client-controlled headers. Any caller can set x-sync-partner-role=district-admin and a truthy x-sync-partner-hint to obtain 'elevated' access in the staff-summary endpoint.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: delegateGradingRoleAction writes the user-supplied 'role' string directly to the enrollment without validating it against an allowlist (the revoke counterpart restrict to teaching_assistant/student). An instructor can assign the 'instructor' role to any roster member, escalating them to co-manager.

Hardcoded fallback JWT secret 'dev-vendor-feed-secret' is used when VENDOR_FEED_SECRET is unset. In a misconfigured production deployment this well-known secret lets attackers forge vendor-feed tokens.
Hardcoded fallback JWT secret 'dev-guardian-portal-secret' is used when GUARDIAN_PORTAL_SECRET is unset, allowing forged guardian access codes.
Hardcoded fallback JWT secret 'dev-report-card-secret' is used when REPORT_CARD_SECRET is unset, allowing forged report-card links.
Hardcoded fallback JWT secret 'dev-enrollment-invite-secret' is used when INVITE_SECRET is unset, allowing forged enrollment invite codes.
